text: Hi, this is Kenji from Binance Research and today I will be recapping our global markets overview for October. You can find this report and all of our Latest archived@research.binance.com the first of our research views is an update from Devcon 5 hosted in Osaka, Japan on October 8th at Devcon. Attendees were notified that phase one of ETH 2.0, including the launch of the Beacon chain, is tentatively scheduled for 2020, with full transition potentially taking another three to four years. Eth 2.0's launch is still highly anticipated as network congestion indicators have remained. While the Ethereum network utilization ratio fell from an average of 94% in September down to an average of 70% in October, it is still considerably high. Amidst the number of proposals and discussions at DEVCON 5, the plasma group presented a potential interim solution to Ethereum's scaling issues. The presented concept was the state channel variant, also known as optimistic rollup. Additional common points of interest included sharding, guaranteeing composability and using proof of stake based consensus algorithms. We have seen proof of stake and staking become increasingly relevant in recent months with $8 billion in crypto activity and a total market size of roughly $15.4 billion. Our full report titled the Rise of Staking can be found on our Binance Research website. In other news, Telegram delayed their long awaited launch of the Telegram Open Network from the end of October to the first quarter of 2020. Projects are gearing up for the announced launch of MakerDAO's multicollateral DAI on November 18th and during the last week of October. Bitcoin's price spiked on October 25th when the BTC USDT spot price increased by more than 30% in 15 hours, reaching a temporary high of 10,370 before closing the month at around 9,200. This movement marked Bitcoin's second most volatile day in the last two years, driving a monthly price change of 13.96%. Moving on to global markets of the largest exchange assets by market cap, Bitcoin, xrp, Bitcoin Cash, Binance, Coin and eos secured double digit gains while holding strong exchange volumes in October. The monthly top three gainers on Binance.com were Lend, RLC and Chz, while the monthly top three with the greatest decline in price were band, beam and NPXs. In October, the Bitcoin trading dominance held above 40% at relatively high levels compared to the first few months of 2019. Meanwhile, the Bitcoin market dominance remained around 65 to 70% in October. In October we saw three new base assets listed, including Blockstack, a decentralized computing network and app ecosystem nkn, the winner of the October community listing vote and kava. Binance USD continued its stablecoin push with six base asset listing pairs added on October 21st and we had one fiat currency listing of the Nigerian Naira NGN added to the platform with pairs against BTC, BUSD and BNB. Regarding Binance DEX on chain markets, we saw 12 new pairs listed, including several new stablecoins and notable assets, reaching a total of 113 actively listed pairs. Bitcoin Cash and XRP were Both tokenized as BEP2 assets and listed in October. For Bitcoin Cash, it was listed against BNB while XRP was listed against busd. Nexo was also listed, making it one of the largest assets from a circulating supply perspective to be listed on Binance Chain. Nexo has been one of the largest contributors to Binance Tech's total volumes since its listing. This past month also marked the successful completion of the Binance Chain Archimedes upgrade, one of the most notable features being the introduction of BEP3 where atomic swaps between Binance Chain and other smart contract supporting blockchains can now be conducted. Binance derivative markets, especially the Perpetual Futures BTC USDT contract, had a spectacular rise in daily volumes from the start of October's 250 million up to a peak of $2 billion on October 26th. Since October 3rd, features volumes have remained consistently higher than Binance.com's spot volumes. As a result of this increased demand and recently released features such as low latency services for large clients on the borrowing and lending markets, five new assets have been added for margin Trading, busd, bat, iost, Vet and qtum. Meanwhile, subscriptions now referred to as fixed deposits have continued while flexible deposits have been added with variable rates being much lower than fixed rates. Our final section is Views from Binance Trading.
